headline: Trump-Xi Beijing summit goes LIVE May 13 with Musk + Jensen Huang on Air Force One — first US presidential China visit in nearly a decade; Trump urging Xi to 'open up' China to US business; Musk the only Tesla CEO ever to accompany a US President to Beijing; for Tesla, FSD approval remains the primary negotiation objective — China is Tesla's largest untapped FSD subscriber market; Nvidia chip export regime, rare earth supply chains, and AI governance also on the agenda; summit runs May 13–15 with markets watching for breakthrough or disappointment; TSLA pre-market +0.24% at $434.50 as summit optimism partially offsets prior session decline (Financial Express / BBC / Reuters)

TSLA closes -2.60% at $433.45 on May 12 — three overhangs converge: (1) Panasonic battery production delays threatening Cybercab/Semi/Megapack 3 ramp, (2) Reuters investigation into Austin robotaxi wait times, (3) hot CPI print reinforcing higher-for-longer rate fears; stock had surged 28% in the prior month, making it vulnerable to any negative confluence; intraday low near $422; bull thesis intact — China summit and unsupervised fleet ramp remain the near-term binary catalysts (247wallst / invezz / Yahoo Finance)

Battery pack capacity flagged as Tesla's #1 production bottleneck in SEC filings — Panasonic 4680 delays add new risk to Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and Megapack 3 ramp timelines, all targeted for volume production in 2026; 247wallst analysis confirms Tesla's own language in filings: 'Battery pack capacity continues to be the limiting factor on vehicle production ramp'; 4680 at Giga Texas is at 40 GWh annual capacity but yield rates still below mass-production targets; Panasonic's commercial 4680 ramp has slipped multiple times since 2022; Tesla sourcing 2170 cells from Panasonic/CATL as hedge but Cybercab's structural pack requires 4680 (247wallst / Tesla 10-Q)

Waymo recalls all 3,791 U.S. robotaxis after autonomous vehicle drives straight into San Antonio floodwaters — OTA software fix deployed fleet-wide; incident highlights weather/edge-case perception failures as an industry-wide AV risk; Tesla faces the same challenge but benefits from competitor's public safety scrutiny shifting regulatory attention; recall follows Reuters investigation into Tesla's own robotaxi availability constraints published same day (Reuters / Electrek / Bloomberg)

Tesla FSD gains new European foothold — Ireland's Department of Transport confirms active engagement with Tesla and the National Standards Authority of Ireland (NSAI) ahead of potential FSD Supervised approval; follows Netherlands (April) and Sweden (April) greenlights; Tesla targeting broader EU deployment 'as early as summer 2026'; harmonized EU-wide clearance requires 15/27 member states — next Technical Committee vote: July 2026 (Teslarati / RTE)

Reuters investigation: Tesla robotaxi faces Texas-sized wait times — ~50 vehicles in Austin vs. Waymo's 250+; Dallas reporter spent 2 hours on a 20-min trip; Houston app canceled bookings with no car available for 30+ min; Austin: zero cars available in 27% of checks, 15+ min waits half the time; Electrek argues 'convenience issues' mask the real constraint — Musk admitted on Q1 earnings call that SAFETY validation is what limits fleet expansion, not operations; 25 total unsupervised vehicles across all three Texas cities (Reuters / Electrek)

Austin robotaxi unsupervised ride rate hits 66.7% — 28 of 42 rides in last 7 days with no safety driver; 50 active rider vehicles + 38 Cybercabs in test fleet; up from 59.0% on May 8 and 27.8% on May 6; fleet now operating unsupervised during evening hours for first time; pace of autonomous operational maturity accelerating sharply; three-week trajectory: 27.8% → 59.0% → 66.7% (robotaxitracker.com / Teslarati)

Tesla China retail sales -10% YoY in April (25,956 units) — domestic retail -15% YoY; the widely-reported +36% 'surge' was wholesale/export-inflated (Giga Shanghai output including European and APAC exports, NOT Chinese consumer purchases); Q1 2026 China retail was -16% YoY with January alone crashing -45%; on current trajectory, Tesla risks falling behind Xiaomi in China market share by end of 2026; bear signal directly contradicting the China delivery recovery thesis (Electrek / CnEVPost)
